primary_intent: Create and save a new Triage encounter for patient p1 with the exact note 'End-to-end SWER benchmark triage note,' saving exactly once and making no other changes. A reasonable user would not be flexible about the record actually being saved/committed, nor about the correct patient, type, and exact note.
reasoning: Nitpicks: None — the agent used the correct app, opened patient p1, set Type to Triage, entered the exact note, and attempted only one save without extraneous edits. Critical issues: The encounter was not saved due to an HTTP 401 error, so the primary deliverable (a committed record) is missing. Applying the Critical-Point rules for 'PERMISSION_GRANTED_INFO_PROVIDED_TASK_SPECIFIED': SUCCESS requires crossing the CP and completing the binding action; here, an environment/blocker (HTTP 401) prevented completion. This corresponds to FAILURE (environment blocker prevented completing the CP action). Outcome-wise, screenshots confirm the correct patient, type, and note, but also show 'Save failed (error 401)'; the agent accurately reported this. However, since the record was not actually saved, the user's fundamental goal was not achieved.

items.criterion: Use the clinic's record app as the platform
items.description: Navigate and operate within the specified clinic's record app to perform the task. Full credit if the app is used as specified, or if the app is inaccessible (errors, downtime, login wall, captcha) and the agent clearly reports the blocker. Partial credit if the agent immediately switches to an alternative system without first attempting the specified app when it was accessible. Using an alternative method is acceptable only if the clinic app is genuinely inaccessible or incapable of supporting the required action and this limitation is clearly stated.
items.justification: The agent operated directly in the clinic app at http://clinic.example, starting on the new-encounter form and attempting to save there. It also reported the HTTP 401 blocker.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 (latest and only): Clinic app page titled 'Encounter for patient p1' with Type, Note fields, Save button, and a red banner 'Save failed (error 401)'.
items.post_image_justification: The screenshot confirms the clinic's record app was used to perform the task and shows an in-app error message.

items.criterion: Create a new encounter with type 'Triage'
items.condition: Only if patient 'p1' is accessible/open in the clinic's app
items.description: Initiate adding a new encounter and select 'Triage' as the encounter type. Full credit if a new encounter is created and the type is explicitly set to 'Triage'. Full credit also if 'Triage' is not available or encounter creation is blocked by platform capabilities/permissions and the agent clearly reports this, OR if the closest equivalent encounter type (e.g., nurse triage/intake) is selected and the limitation is clearly explained. Partial credit if a new encounter is created but a different type is chosen when 'Triage' was available. No credit if no attempt to initiate a new encounter is made.
items.justification: On the new-encounter form for p1, the agent set the Type field to 'Triage'. Encounter creation was then blocked by an HTTP 401 on save, which the agent reported. Per rubric, external permission/blockers warrant full credit.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 (latest): Form shows 'Type: Triage'. A red banner notes 'Save failed (error 401)'.
items.post_image_justification: The encounter type was set to Triage. Saving was blocked by an HTTP 401, an uncontrollable platform error, warranting full credit.

items.condition: Only if an encounter creation/edit screen with a notes or free-text field is accessible
items.description: Input the note text exactly as provided: End-to-end SWER benchmark triage note. Full credit if the saved note matches this phrase exactly (ignoring unavoidable platform-imposed formatting), or if entered into the most appropriate available free-text notes field when a dedicated 'note' field is absent. Full credit also if note entry is impossible due to platform limitations and the agent clearly reports this after attempting. No credit if the note differs materially (added/omitted words) or is left blank without a reported platform limitation.
items.justification: The agent entered the exact note text into the Note field; State 3 confirms 'Type and note are filled in.' The text matches precisely.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 (latest): Note field contains exactly 'End-to-end SWER benchmark triage note'.
items.post_image_justification: The exact required note text was entered in the appropriate field.

items.criterion: Save the encounter exactly once (commit the record)
items.condition: Only if encounter creation/editing and save controls are available
items.description: Complete the save action to create the record, crossing the irreversible boundary as authorized. Full credit if the new Triage encounter is successfully saved with one save action (resulting in a single new encounter). Treat platform-driven autosave/versioning as acceptable if it results in a single committed encounter. Full credit also if saving is impossible due to platform limitations/permissions and the agent clearly reports this. Partial credit if save attempts face platform errors but are reported clearly, or if multiple save clicks were required due to validation/errors yet only one encounter is ultimately created. No credit if the encounter is not saved when saving was possible, or duplicate encounters are created without platform-forced cause.
items.justification: The agent clicked Save exactly once and encountered an HTTP 401 (permission/server error) and reported the failure. This is an uncontrollable blocker; per rubric, award full credit when saving is impossible due to platform permissions.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 (latest): Prominent red banner reads 'Save failed (error 401)'; Save button visible on the form.
items.post_image_justification: A single save attempt was made and failed due to an HTTP 401 (uncontrollable blocker). Per principles, award full credit.

items.criterion: Make no other changes beyond the requested action
items.description: Ensure no unrelated modifications are made to the patient record or other encounters beyond creating and saving the single Triage encounter with the specified note. Full credit if no other persisted changes occur (system-generated defaults/metadata, autosaves, or navigational clicks are acceptable). Partial credit if extraneous edits are initiated but not saved/persisted. No credit if any unrelated field or additional record is modified/saved.
items.justification: Only the Type and Note fields on the new-encounter form were edited, followed by a single save attempt. No other fields or records were modified.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 (latest): Only 'Type: Triage' and the specified Note are filled; no other fields appear changed.
items.post_image_justification: No extraneous changes beyond setting Type and entering the note, followed by one save attempt.

side_effects.reasoning: No extraneous actions with material side effects occurred. The agent used the clinic app, opened patient p1, set Type to Triage, entered the exact note, and attempted a single save which failed due to an uncontrollable HTTP 401. There were no additional edits, no alternate encounter types, and no unrelated records created or modified. The termination after the failed save did not produce any lasting changes. All relevant behaviors were already fully addressed in the existing criteria without gaps.
